MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 27, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR HUFF at 7:05 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Jason Xue from Boy Scout Troop 134 led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager, Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION – ANDREA VONA, PALOS VERDES PENINSULA
  LAND CONSERVANCY

  MAYOR HUFF presented a certificate of recognition to Andrea Vona in recognition of her
  10 years of dedicated service to the Palos Verdes Peninsula community during her tenure
  as Executive Director of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy.

B.  RESOLUTION OF COMMENDATION – CAPTAIN DANIEL BERINGER, LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT

  MAYOR HUFF presented a Resolution of Commendation and City tile plaque to Captain
  Dan Beringer in recognition of his retirement from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department after 30-years of dedicated service and expressing appreciation for his
  service to the City during his tenure as Captain of the Lomita Station.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
 CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
  Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to
  the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-H AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVE.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 13, 2018

  APPROVE AS PRESENTED.

C.  JOINT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF OCTOBER 30, 2018

  APPROVE AS PRESENTED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – NOVEMBER 2018

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

E.  OCTOBER 2018 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

F.  OCTOBER 2018 REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPOT

  RECEIVE AND FILE

G.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 7, 2018

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

H.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR THE FUNDING OF TABER GROVE
  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION COSTS

  AUTHORIZED THE CITY MANGER TO SIGN THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY AND PALOS VERDES PENINSULA
  LAND CONSERVANCY FOR THE FUNDING OF PARK DESIGN AND
  CONSTRUCTION COSTS TO DEVELOP JOHN AND LYNN TABER GROVE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
 PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION  ITEM:  NATURE  CENTER
  REPLACEMENT STUDY CONSULTANT SELECTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into an agreement with Roesling Nakamura
  Terada Architects (RNT) in conjunction with Spurlock Landscape Architects to complete
  a Nature Center Replacement Study for George F Canyon Nature Center.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ, Community Services Director Clark
  clarified that Roesling Nakamura Terada Architects and Spurlock Landscape Architects
  will be working together to complete the scope of work, but the City’s agreement will be
  with RNT with Spurlock serving as a sub-contractor.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she was impressed with examples of
  previous projects included in RNT’s proposal and expressed appreciation to the Park and
  Activities Commission for its diligent work on this project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO FINALIZE
  THE AGREED UPON SCOPE OF WORK AND ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT
  WITH ROESLING NAKAMURA TERADA ARCHITECTS IN CONJUNCTION
  WITH SPURLOCK LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTS IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO
  EXCEED $20,000 TO COMPLETE A NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT
  STUDY FOR GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER ALL TO THE
  SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PARKWAY PLANTINGS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the planting of Bougainvillea vines in
  selected locations along Palos Verdes Drive North.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
   In response to MAYOR HUFF’S inquiry regarding the area between Palos Verdes Drive
  North and Montecillo where the new Butcher properties were developed, Community
  Services Director Clark explained that the area is maintained by the adjacent
  homeowners association’s landscaping contractor.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Community Services Director Clark
  commented that the bougainvillea vines would be planted in more open areas where there
  is ample space away from walking paths and bridle trails. She expressed concern
  regarding the maintenance requirements and hazards associated with bougainvillea and
  inquired as to whether or not any other plants that were considered. Community Services
  Director Clark commented that Bougainvillea is not currently part of the City’s plant
  palette; and it this time, it was the only plant considered based on a suggestion from the
  Mayor. He further reviewed other locations where Bougainvillea currently exists
  throughout the City.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL suggested that it may be better to consider other plant
  varieties to add color; and look at the project from a more holistic approach to include the
  plantings that will need to be done at the conclusion of the Cal Water project on Palos
  Verdes Drive North.

  COUNCILMEMBERS SCHMITZ and ZERUNYAN concurred with MAYOR PRO TEM
  MITCHELL’S comments.

  Following discussion, COUNCIL provided direction to staff as follows:

  STAFF WAS DIRECTED TO RETURN WITH OTHER PLANTING OPTIONS FOR
  ADDING COLOR IN THE PARKWAY PLANTINGS AND SCHEDULE A
  DISCUSSION DURING THE POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION TO CONSIDER
  AN OVERARCHING LANDSCAPE MASTER PLAN FOR PARKWAYS AND
  MEDIANS.

OLD BUSINESS

A.  EXPANSION OF AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER (ALPR) CAMERA SYSTEM

  Recommendation: That the City Council provide direction on expanding the ALPR camera
  system over the next two fiscal years as outlined in options A, B and C. Further, City
  Council may direct staff to return with a final contract for purchase and applicable
  agreements with bordering agencies to implement the ALPR camera expansion project.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Captain Beringer, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Dept. provided a summary of the results
  achieved since the original ALPR cameras were installed in 2016 and commented that
  the ALPR camera system is a helpful tool in fighting crime and provides valuable
  investigative benefits.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
   In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Captain Beringer explained the
  investigative benefits of capturing both ingress and egress.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Deputy Otis explained how the system
  works both from an immediate response and an investigative perspective. Captain
  Beringer provided an example of a situation where the investigative benefits were applied.

  Discussion ensued concerning the stolen vehicle recovery benefits of the ALPR system
  versus the investigative/crime fighting benefits.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that it may be more prudent to consider the
  expansion of the ALPR system for ingress only at this time; and wait until the FLOCK
  program is analyzed under the pilot program to consider egress. Deputy Otis commented
  that the FLOCK system is still being analyzed, but it will likely only provide benefits in
  situations where the vehicle speeds are under 40 mph.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that she concurs with COUNCILMEMBER
  ZERUNYAN’S suggestion to take the more prudent path and install the ALPR cameras
  for ingress only at this time and use the analytics received from the pilot program using
  the FLOCK system to decide how to proceed from there.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she would be supportive of installing the
  cameras for both ingress and egress given the investigative benefits having both
  provides. She noted that she sees the ALPR system and the FLOCK system as separate
  from one another.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that given the increasing law enforcement
  costs associated with the Sheriff’s Department contract, it may be prudent to install the
  ALPR cameras for ingress only at this time in case there are other crime fighting
  measures that need to be implemented.

  Discussion ensued concerning the pros and cons of installing the ALPR cameras for
  ingress only versus both ingress and egress.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN WITH THE FINAL
  CONTRACT WITH VIGILANT AND APPLICABLE AGREEMENTS WITH
  BORDERING AGENCIES TO EXPAND THE ALPR CAMERA SYSTEM OVER THE
  NEXT TWO FISCAL YEARS TO INCLUDE CAMERAS IN ALL FOUR PROPOSED
  LOCATIONS WITH INGRESS ONLY INSTALLATION (OPTION B); AND FURTHER
  BRING THE MATTER BACK FOR DISCUSSION AT THE POLICY DEVELOPMENT
  SESSION TO CONSIDER THE EGRESS OPTION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
 B.  NEIGHBORHOOD CAMERA RIGHT-OF-WAY POLICY AND AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Neighborhood Camera Right-of-
  Way Policy and Agreement which will allow neighborhood cameras to be installed on City
  rights-of-way.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Discussion ensued concerning the relay of data to the Sheriff’s Department.

  MAYOR PRO MITCHELL commented that it would be a good idea to also develop a
  policy for situations where the cameras are installed on private property. She further
  commented that there may be circumstances where the agreement may need to be
  terminated in a situation other than default of the terms; and suggested that a clause be
  added that the agreement can be terminated with good cause.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that based on current California license
  law, the license should be revocable by the licensor at will.

  Discussion ensued concerning the City’s ability to revoke the license and the means by
  which the City may do so.

  Further discussion ensued concerning situations where the cameras may be installed on
  private property. COUNCIL concurred that there is no need to change this policy to
  address cameras on private property.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE NEIGHBORHOOD CAMERA RIGHT-
  OF-WAY POLICY AND AGREEMENT TO ALLOW NEIGHBORHOOD CAMERAS
  TO BE INSTALLED ON CITY RIGHTS-OF-WAY AS AMENDED TO INCLUDE A
  PROVISION TO ALLOW THE CITY TO REVOKE THE LICENSE AT WILL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION NEIGHBORHOOD ENTRYWAY CAMERA GRANT
  PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the HOA Neighborhood Entryway
  Camera Grant Program, formal application and allocate grant funds in the amount of
  $15,000 with the appropriate budget adjustment.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ Administrative Analyst Slawson explained
  that whether the camera is installed on private property or in the public right-of-way, the
  HOA would be required to execute the appropriate agreements relative to that installation.
  Discussion ensued concerning the requirements of the various agreements.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
   Vatche Shirikjian and Fred Tramm, residents of the Westfield Neighborhood, addressed
  the COUNCIL regarding neighborhood entryway cameras providing information on the
  camera system that the Westfield Neighborhood is currently researching; and requesting
  that the Westfield Neighborhood be included in the Neighborhood Entryway Camera
  Grant program because they believe that the camera would not only benefit the Westfield
  Neighborhood, but the City of Rolling Hills Estates as well.

  Discussion ensued concerning the camera options available as part of the HOA
  Neighborhood Entryway Grant Program. Assistant to the City Manager Davis clarified
  that at this time, there are only two cameras included in the program; but in the future,
  other cameras could be added.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that at this time, the grant program is only
  available to neighborhoods in the City of Rolling Hills Estates.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that if Mr. Shirikjian and Mr. Tramm wish to
  receive funding to support the Westfield Neighborhood entryway camera program, they
  should submit a proposal to staff and it will be agendized for consideration on a future
  COUNCIL agenda for discussion as to whether or not to expand the City’s grant program
  to include locations outside the City.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE HOA NEIGHBORHOOD
  ENTRYWAY CAMERA GRANT PROGRAM AND FORMAL APPLICATION WITH
  THE APPROPRIATE AMENDMENTS; AND ALLOCATE GRANT FUNDS IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $15,000 WITH THE APPROPRIATE BUDGET ADJUSTMENT

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

D.  PILOT PROGRAM (NEIGHBORHOOD ENTRYWAY CAMERAS)

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) approve a Pilot Neighborhood Camera
  Program for camera placement at the Montecillo Neighborhood; 2) allocate funds in the
  amount of $2,000 for purchase of the camera for one-year; and 3) direct staff to enter into
  a contract with FLOCK to establish the pilot program in partnership with the Sheriff’s
  Department’s Technology and Support Division subject to review and approval by the City
  Attorney.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ regarding the cost of this program
  compared to the HOA grant program, Administrative Analyst Slawson explained that this
  is an agreement for a pilot program between the City and FLOCK not the neighborhood.

  Discussion ensued concerning the parameters of the pilot program, the costs associated
  with the one-year program and ownership of the camera and the data.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
   COUNCIL expressed concern regarding data analytics; ownership of the camera and the
  data; and the terms of the agreement.

  Following discussion, COUNCIL tabled consideration of this matter and provided direction
  to staff as follows:

  STAFF WAS DIRECTED TO BRING BACK THE FLOCK CONTRACT FOR CITY
  COUNCIL REVIEW AND DISCUSSION.

E.  PERSONAL PROPERTY GRANT PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) approve the creation of a Personal Property
  Grant Program and the allocation of funds in the amount of $5,000; and 2) direct staff to
  enter into a contract with RING to participate in the discount program subject to review
  and approval by the City Attorney.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN stated his opposition to this program commenting that
  this is something residents can do on their own and the City does not need to participate.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she too is opposed to this program
  because, compared to previous items discussed that benefit neighborhoods, this is
  personal device and the City should not provide monetary support for personal items.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ concurred.

  COUNCIILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he is opposed as well because of
  the limited offering.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL NOT MOVE FORWARD WITH THE PERSONAL
  PROPERTY GRANT PROGRAM.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
 CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to other
  Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently active Council
  Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special districts and/or
  joint powers authorities and their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN provided an update on the CPA’s rate setting process and
noted that the City’s Environmental Advisory Committee will have further discussions regarding
the default rate tier at its January meeting.

MAYOR HUFF noted that the SBCCOG is hosting an Energy Leader Recognition at the Nakano
Theater in Torrance on Thursday from 11:30 a.m. – 1:30 p.m. and invited all Councilmembers
to attend.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently pending
  projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration and/or make
  announcements of interest to the public.

MAYOR HUFF reminded everyone that the Holiday Parade of Lights and reception will be held
this Saturday, December 1 and invited all to attend.

CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

ADJOURNMENT

At 9:32 p.m. MAYOR HUFF formally adjourned the City Council meeting. An adjourned meeting
of the City Council will be held on Tuesday, December 11, 2018 at 6:00 p.m. at City Hall, 4045
Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California for the purpose of conducting
Commission/Committee interviews. The next regular meeting of the City council will be held on
Tuesday, December 11, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  Assistant City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  9
NOVEMBER 27, 2018
